profile.reading:
This is a Digital Realty facility at 3825/3855 Northeast Aloclek Drive, Hillsboro, OR, per mapping data. Digital Realty's own property listing shows PDX10 at 3825 NW Aloclek Street, Hillsboro, OR (48,000 square feet); the directional discrepancy (NE vs NW) in the two records was not resolved this session, so this entry is treated as a likely but not fully confirmed match to PDX10 rather than assumed identical.

Digital Realty Trust (NYSE: DLR, SEC CIK 1297996), headquartered at 2323 Bryan Street, Dallas, Texas, reported 310 data centers worldwide as of December 31, 2025, 221 wholly owned or consolidated and 89 in unconsolidated joint ventures, about 57.6 million rentable square feet across more than 55 metro markets including 118 US facilities, per its FY2025 Form 10-K filed with the SEC. The company operates as a colocation and wholesale landlord rather than running its own compute, distinguishing it from hyperscaler tenants such as AWS, Google, or Meta, also tracked in this registry.

This building is part of Digital Realty's Portland metro footprint, concentrated in Hillsboro, a Portland suburb that also hosts major semiconductor manufacturing and, per Digital Realty's own metro page, named properties PDX10 and PDX12 along Aloclek Drive and Schaaf Street. Portland General Electric serves most of the Hillsboro data center market, and Oregon offers enterprise-zone property tax abatements that Washington County and the City of Hillsboro have used to attract large industrial and data center investment. Digital Realty markets its Portland properties under its PlatformDIGITAL brand within its global interconnection and colocation platform.

Digital Realty's FY2025 Form 10-K discloses portfolio metrics by region and metro market rather than per-building specifics for any US facility; this pattern of aggregate, not per-building, disclosure is consistent across every Digital Realty property researched by this registry this session, and is not unique to this entry.

reading.body:
PDX10 is a 48,000-square-foot facility in Hillsboro, Oregon with an aggregator-sourced capacity figure of approximately 10 MW that has not been confirmed by Digital Realty directly. At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, this would suggest around 250 racks, though this translation rests on the unconfirmed 10 MW figure and assumes no power reserved for non-compute uses. The facility's actual IT load, power delivery capacity, and tenant mix are not published.

Oregon has 133 mapped data centers but only 8 publish power capacity figures totaling 156.6 MW across the state. PDX10 does not appear in the published-capacity ranking because its 10 MW figure lacks operator confirmation. If confirmed, it would rank ninth in the state by published capacity, placing it among the small fraction of Oregon facilities with disclosed power specifications.

The published specifications contain no certifications, SLA commitments, power source disclosures, cooling technology, or grid interconnection details. Digital Realty's own site provides only the facility address and floor area. Without operator-published power capacity or infrastructure specifications, PDX10 cannot be assessed for relevance to large-scale AI workloads.
